pool.text: Sir Richard Burton published the first written description of the Kibuga in his book.
John Speke arrived in Buganda when the capital was located at Bandabarogo.
Henry Morton Stanley met Kabaka Mutesa I at Lubaga Hill.
Protestant missionaries from the Church Mission Society arrived and were allocated Namirembe Hill.
Frederick Lugard signed a British protection treaty while the capital was at Mengo Hill.
Mengo Senior School opened at Namirembe hill as the first Western education school.
Sir Albert Ruskin Cook opened Mengo Hospital as the first Western-style health facility.
The Missionary Sisters of Our Lady of Africa founded Lubaga Hospital on Lubaga Hill.
Regents and officials signed the Buganda Agreement with Sir Harry Johnston.
The Kampala boundary was set as a three-mile radius from Nakasero Fort.
Kampala Township received its first land-use plan with a specific population count.
The Uganda Railway line reached Kampala after thirty-five years of construction.
Sir Philip Mitchel switched on Kampala and Uganda's first electric street lights.
Henry Kendall's third physical plan expanded the area of Kampala.
Uganda gained independence and Kampala was granted city status as the new capital.
Kampala boundaries expanded to incorporate surrounding townships and areas.
The Battle of Kampala took place during the Ugandan Bush War.
The Kampala Capital City Authority Act gave the Ugandan Government more administrative control.
Google launched its first Wi-Fi network in Kampala in December.
The Allied Democratic Forces carried out suicide bombings near the central police station and parliament.
